findings.rule: Tolerances tighter than a normal machining process can hold
findings.reasoning: Dimension D1 specifies 15 ±0.003 mm (6 µm total tolerance band). This is an IT2-grade tolerance that requires lapping or jig-grinding, which is disproportionate for a mild-steel pipe clamp block and extremely costly to produce.
findings.correction: Relax the tolerance on D1 to a value achievable by standard milling or grinding (e.g., ±0.05 or ±0.1 mm), unless a precision dowel fit is truly required and justified.

findings.rule: Functional hole diameter left with no tolerance or fit class
findings.reasoning: The two Ø6.4 holes (D7 / F6) have no tolerance specified. A 6.4 mm diameter strongly implies a clearance hole for an M6 fastener; without a defined tolerance or fit class, the shop cannot guarantee the bolt will pass through or that the clamp will locate correctly.
findings.correction: Add an explicit tolerance or fit class to D7 (e.g., Ø6.4 H13, or Ø6.5 ±0.1 for clearance) so the hole function is unambiguous.
